title: Night view of Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing entrance with illuminated facade
objects_and_counts: Two tall streetlamp posts with spherical yellow-orange globes are visible in the foreground: one near image center-left and one center-right; both lamp globes are lit and the poles are fully visible.

At least two people are visible on the left side of the image walking along the covered walkway; they are distant and partially illuminated (one closer to the camera near the left edge and another further back).

A glass-fronted entrance/ground-floor façade spans the central portion of the image; multiple vertical glass panels form the facade (a visible minimum of six distinct full-height glass panels on the ground floor can be seen, with additional partial panels at the edges).

A large rectangular dark object (appears to be a covered board or screen) is positioned in the main entrance opening; three small warm lights or reflections (orange-yellow) are visible on or in front of that dark object.
An interior illuminated 'EXIT' sign is visible above an inner doorway inside the entrance lobby area.
A continuous illuminated light band or backlit panel runs along the upper facade above the glass panels, forming a canopy-like luminous strip across the entrance.
spatial_relations: The illuminated upper facade band with the text 'TAM WING FAN INNOVATION WING' runs horizontally above the ground-floor glass panels and main entrance.

Two lit globe streetlamps stand in the paved forecourt in front of the building; one is positioned approximately center-left in front of the main entrance and the other is center-right, slightly in front of the right side of the entrance.
The main glass entrance is set back beneath the illuminated upper band; the large dark rectangular object is located within that recessed entrance area.
A covered walkway extends to the left of the entrance; the two distant people are on that walkway toward the left side of the image.
Windows on the right side of the building are separated from the main entrance by a vertical structural column and face the forecourt at a lower elevation than the illuminated upper band.
colours_and_materials: The upper facade band is bright white and backlit, producing a cool white illumination.
The streetlamp globes emit a warm yellow-orange light that casts warm tones on the brick pavement.
The forecourt ground is paved with reddish-brown or orange brick tiles visible under the warm lamp light.
The entrance and facade include large clear glass panels with visible metal framing (frames appear dark/grey in the available light).
The large rectangular object in the entrance appears dark (black) and non-reflective except for three warm light points or reflections.
uncertainties: Smaller text adjacent to 'TAM WING FAN INNOVATION WING' (appearing to be Chinese characters) is present but not legible at this resolution.
Vertical gold-coloured text on the left column of the entrance is visible but the characters are not legible from the image.
A small sign on the lower right wall of the forecourt is visible but its text is unreadable.

The exact count of glass panels is given as a visible minimum (at least six full-height panels); additional panels are partially cropped or obscured and the full count cannot be determined from this image.
The identity of the large dark rectangular object in the entrance (covered board, screen, or other) cannot be determined from appearance alone.
People are described by visible presence only; no identifying information or names is provided or inferred.
